claims.claim: Decolonization is the process by which colonized peoples ended European imperial rule and formed independent states, becoming a worldwide wave in roughly the two decades after 1945.

Decolonization accelerated after World War II because the imperial powers were militarily and economically weakened, nationalist movements had mass support and experienced leaders, and a new international climate (Atlantic Charter 1941, Fifth Pan-African Congress October 1945, the UN) favored self-determination.

The UN General Assembly adopted Resolution 1514 (XV), the Declaration on the Granting of Independence to Colonial Countries and Peoples, on 14 December 1960 (by 89 to 0 with 9 abstentions), affirming self-determination and calling for a speedy and unconditional end to colonialism.

In 1947 British India was partitioned into two independent states, Pakistan (independence celebrated 14 August 1947) and India (15 August 1947); the partition displaced roughly fifteen million people, and scholarly estimates of deaths range from several hundred thousand to as many as two million.
Ghana, led by Kwame Nkrumah, became the first sub-Saharan colony to gain independence, on 6 March 1957.
1960 is called the 'Year of Africa' because seventeen African nations became independent in that single year, most of them former French colonies, along with the Belgian Congo and British Nigeria.

Paths to independence ranged from negotiated transfers of power to armed liberation struggles; Algeria's National Liberation Front fought France from 1954 to 1962, ending with the Evian Accords and independence on 5 July 1962, after which more than a million residents of European descent left.

Newly independent states inherited arbitrary colonial borders, economies structured for extraction and export to the former colonizer, Cold War entanglement, and neocolonialism (continued foreign economic and political control despite formal independence), a term associated with Kwame Nkrumah.

At the Bandung Conference in April 1955, representatives of twenty-nine Asian and African countries met to cooperate and avoid dependence on either Cold War bloc, laying groundwork for the Non-Aligned Movement (leaders included Nehru, Nasser, and Sukarno).

conflictingEvidence.issue: Death toll of the 1947 Partition of India
positions: Commonly cited range of roughly 200,000 to 1 million deaths for March 1947-January 1948
Wider scholarly range up to about 2 million dead
conflictingEvidence.resolution: The lesson states the figure as a range (several hundred thousand up to as many as two million) rather than a single number, and frames displacement (~15 million) as the more firmly established figure, per Britannica and general scholarship.

positions: Some recent research suggests over 18 million migrated
conflictingEvidence.resolution: The lesson uses the widely cited 'roughly fifteen million' figure and notes it as an approximation, avoiding overstated precision.
